reason: r19 moves the clip box to the mask's own enter handler and adds a liveness check. r18 (NRO 55340cfbec4fbdc176be57d3ac22356945c4f431f882eb784b362426a1e23330, run on Eden 2026-10-24, installed bytes matching) completed the first insertion this mod has had: the mask, a 5-word object array and a 9-record draw block all published, and the user reported the gauge missing. Its 425 clip readbacks show why: 376 of 383 sane lines have left == right, top/bottom ours and the width gone, with flags 0x1. The rectangle at mask+0xb0..+0xbc is derived state the game rewrites from the node's quad on every layout, and a node the animation row has no entry for has quad width 0, so a box written at the walker's entry never reaches the scissor. r19 writes the authored pair, the position pair, the rectangle and the enable bit in main+0xa4ba94's hook, in the call that applies them, and stops writing when the mask's parent link no longer points at the captured root: r18's last 90 seconds show writes into a freed mask, the root destructor having fired zero times across six sessions. The rest of the insertion is unchanged and is evidenced by that run: the mask built by the class factory main+0xa4b6cc, the object array grown through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator with instance+0xd8 and root+0xa0 published, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic (sized from the halfwords at row+8: 3 objects, 16 sequences, record area 56 = 7 records, grown to 72 = 9), and the native linkers for the tree. r14 (NRO 6e061c70779cfb3a306835030256012e50dd19fdbeeae36d4d4635c331d35b8d) remains the failed insertion run whose two failures (the map length and the cache record area) the expansions answer. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r19 writes the clip box inside the mask's enter handler (main+0xa4ba94) and drops its addresses when the mask's links are gone. r18 ran once on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 55340cfbec4fbdc176be57d3ac22356945c4f431f882eb784b362426a1e23330): the insertion completed (mask 0x48003060, 5-entry map, 9-record cache) and the user reported the gauge missing; 376 of 383 probe lines show a zero-width scissor box and the last 90 s show writes into a freed mask. r17 ran clean the same day with its gate stopping the insertion; r16/r15 ran clean on 2026-10-23; r14 ran once and failed as reported.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r19 has not been run. The one completed insertion (r18) hid the gauge: the clip box arrived zero-width because the mask's rectangle is the game's layout's to compute; the enter-hook write site and the link-based liveness check have no runtime evidence, and the mask's teardown is unproven, the root-destructor hook having fired zero times in six sessions
